item.title: Kentucky child killer walks free as family says justice failed despite years of legal fights
item.description: Ronald Exantus walked free after serving his sentence for the 2015 home invasion that killed 6-year-old Logan Tipton, despite Logan's Law reforms.
item.content:encoded:
The Kentucky father whose 6-year-old son was stabbed to death while sleeping says the man found not guilty by reason of insanity in the killing received "a slap on the wrist" after being released from prison July 29 upon completing his sentence for assaulting three surviving family members.

Ronald Exantus was released from Kentucky Department of Corrections custody on July 29 after completing the sentence imposed for assaulting Logan Tipton's father and sisters during the 2015 home invasion that left the 6-year-old dead.

The case stunned Kentucky after prosecutors said Exantus broke into the Tipton family's home on Dec. 7, 2015, and fatally stabbed 6-year-old Logan Tipton while he slept. Logan's father and two sisters were also stabbed but survived the attack. A jury later found Exantus not guilty by reason of insanity on murder and burglary charges but guilty but mentally ill on assault charges involving the surviving family members.

The assault convictions resulted in the prison sentence he completed last week, reigniting outrage from the Tipton family and renewed questions about Kentucky's criminal justice system.

FLORIDA AG SEEKS JUDGE'S IMPEACHMENT AFTER BABY DROWNING COVID INSANITY ACQUITTAL

"The judge and jury gave this monster a slap on the wrist while handing down a life sentence to my family," Logan's father, Dean Tipton, wrote on Facebook after Exantus' release. "Make sure to lock your doors and keep an eye out for baby killers. He will be released today. Watch your house, your neighbors house, your kids, your neighbors kids. He could be coming to your town. Kentucky justice at its finest."

According to the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Exantus completed the sentence imposed by the court after receiving sentence credits required under Kentucky law.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

"Ronald Exantus has served the sentence issued by the Woodford Circuit Court and has been released," the department told Fox News Digital. "He is no longer in the custody of the Department of Corrections."

Corrections officials emphasized that juries and courts determine an offender's sentence, while the department is responsible for calculating that sentence under Kentucky law, including applying any earned statutory sentence credits.

Once Exantus reached his legally calculated sentence expiration date, the agency said it no longer had authority to keep him incarcerated.

The department also stressed that the Kentucky Parole Board "did not release Exantus, and he was not released early."

Exantus was briefly released on mandatory reentry supervision in October 2025 before moving to Florida, where authorities said he violated the conditions of his supervision by failing to register as a convicted felon.

He was returned to Kentucky after the violation, and the Parole Board revoked his mandatory reentry supervision, ordering him back to prison. The department said he ultimately remained incarcerated until completing his sentence on July 29.

NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman said his office worked alongside prosecutors, law enforcement and corrections officials to keep Exantus incarcerated for as long as the law allowed.

In a November 2025 letter to the Kentucky Parole Board, Coleman urged board members to revoke Exantus' mandatory reentry supervision after Exantus violated its conditions in Florida and required him to serve the remainder of his sentence in prison.

"The public good and common sense demand nothing less," Coleman wrote, calling Logan Tipton's killing "every parent's worst nightmare."

The Parole Board ultimately revoked Exantus's mandatory reentry supervision and ordered him back to prison after finding he violated the terms of his supervision.

Ahead of Exantus's scheduled release, the Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet also notified the trial judge, Commonwealth's Attorney Kelli Kearney and defense counsel that they could pursue involuntary hospitalization proceedings before his sentence expired if they believed it was appropriate under Kentucky law.

The Department of Corrections said it lacked the legal authority to continue holding Exantus once he completed his sentence unless another lawful basis for detention was established.

In a November 2025 interview with WKYT, Coleman said "the system failed the Tipton family," while pledging to pursue every legal avenue available to keep Exantus incarcerated.

CALIFORNIA MOM RIPS NEWSOM-BACKED 'DIVERSION PROGRAM' THAT APPEARS TO BENEFIT HER SON'S KILLER

Public outrage over Logan’s case helped spur Kentucky lawmakers to pass House Bill 422, known as Logan’s Law, which Gov. Andy Beshear signed in April.

The law revised Kentucky’s insanity defense and mandatory reentry supervision rules in response to issues raised by Exantus’ case. But because it does not apply retroactively, it had no effect on Exantus'sentence or July 29 release.

State Rep. Daniel Fister, who helped champion the legislation, called Exantus' release "heartbreaking" and vowed to continue working with the Tipton family to strengthen Kentucky's criminal laws.

"My heart breaks yet again for the Tipton family and our community as we are once again forced to endure the pain and uncertainty caused by Ronald Exantus," Fister told Fox News Digital.

NORTH CAROLINA TEACHER'S KILLING REIGNITES SCRUTINY OF ROY COOPER'S CRIMINAL JUSTICE RECORD IN SENATE RACE

"No family should have to endure this kind of trauma, and every Kentuckian deserves confidence that our justice system will protect innocent victims and hold violent offenders accountable."

Fister said Logan's Law was "an important step forward" but promised lawmakers would continue pursuing reforms to better protect Kentucky families.

"We owe it to Logan's memory and to every family across the Commonwealth to continue pursuing reforms that put the safety of innocent Kentuckians first," he said.

Fister also said Exantus' release underscores broader concerns about Kentucky's criminal justice system, arguing that delays in implementing provisions of House Bill 5 have allowed some violent offenders to become eligible for parole earlier than lawmakers intended.

DEVASTATED MOTHER BLAMES SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICIES AFTER CAREER CRIMINAL IS CHARGED IN SON’S DEATH

"That is deeply troubling for victims and their families, who deserve confidence that violent criminals will be held fully accountable," he said.

State Rep. T.J. Roberts, who also helped author Logan's Law, called Exantus's release "a gross miscarriage of justice."

"Once again, Kentucky's judiciary has failed the Tipton family," Roberts told Fox News Digital. "The monster who killed Logan Tipton should spend the rest of his life in prison, at a minimum, and his release is a gross miscarriage of justice. The Tipton family, all of Kentucky, and all of America deserve so much better than what this government offers to the innocent."

Roberts noted that the U.S. Constitution prohibits lawmakers from retroactively increasing criminal penalties, meaning Logan's Law could not be applied to Exantus after his conviction.

GIANNO CALDWELL: FOUR YEARS AFTER MY BROTHER’S MURDER, I’M MARCHING FOR JUSTICE

Calling Logan's Law "a great first step," Roberts said he plans to introduce additional legislation that would expand the availability of life without parole for murder convictions, strengthen victim notification requirements and further protect Kentuckians from violent offenders.

"I intend to file legislation to ensure our justice system protects the innocent, not violent offenders," he said.

Roberts also offered a message directly to the Tipton family.

"I want the Tipton family to know they have my support and the support of millions of people who have heard their story," he said. "God is with them, and we will not let Logan's life be forgotten."

BODYCAM FOOTAGE FUELS BACKLASH AFTER POLICE HANDCUFF DYING STABBING VICTIM

For Tipton, Exantus' release reopened wounds that have never healed.

"Knowing that this monster gets to walk free and live his life, while I lay in this bed and my baby boy is in the grave," he wrote. "This may be my breaking point."

Although Logan's Law has now taken effect, Tipton said he believes Kentucky must go further.

"So I've come to terms that even though we got Logans Law passed it is still not enough," he wrote. "Violent criminals should not be able to knock so much time off their sentence."

"Our judicial system as a whole needs to be over hauled and I am gonna fight for more change."

Despite helping inspire Logan's Law, the Tipton family says its fight is far from over. The family has launched a GoFundMe to help pay for attorneys as they pursue additional legal remedies and continue pushing for further criminal justice reforms.

"We turned our deepest grief into a fierce, relentless battle to change the law so no other family would ever have to suffer the way we have," the family wrote on the fundraising page. But while Logan's Law was signed this year, they noted it "does not retroactively stop our son's killer from being released."

"The fight is not over and we need your help," the family added.

item.title: Rosie O'Donnell won't worry about FCC, Brendan Carr ahead of Kimmel hosting, doesn't 'pay any heed to them'
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell dismissed FCC Chairman Brendan Carr and his agency as a threat ahead of her upcoming "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" guest hosting stint later this month.
item.content:encoded:
Rosie O'Donnell told Kara Swisher Monday that she isn't worried about the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) or FCC Chairman Brendan Carr ahead of a guest hosting stint on ABC's "Jimmy Kimmel Live!"

The former TV personality discussed her plans for appearing on Kimmel's show on Swisher's podcast. The conversation eventually led to O'Donnell's ongoing feud with President Donald Trump and whether his administration could go after the broadcast.

"Let me ask you, are you worried that Trump, speaking of doing things, he'll obviously be watching you because he's riveted to you in some fashion... Are you worried about any FCC?" Swisher asked. "They went after ABC. They went after ‘The View.’ They're continuing to go after 'The View,' but are you worried about the FCC under Brendan Carr?"

JIMMY KIMMEL REVEALS HE ASKED MAJOR TRUMP CRITIC TO GUEST HOST WHILE HE'S ON VACATION AS A 'SPECIAL TREAT'

"Doing what?" O'Donnell asked.

"Coming after you on the show, for example, doing anything?" Swisher clarified.

"No. What are they going to say? That you can't say that?" O'Donnell said.

Swisher claimed that Carr, whom she referred to as a "moron," was "saying" things like that, but O'Donnell continued to dismiss him as a threat.

"Well, I don't listen to them. I don't pay any heed to them," O'Donnell said.

Though she did not express any concern regarding repercussions for her time as host, O'Donnell revealed that the network had already rejected her Trump-related parody of the "Wizard of Oz" song "If I Only Had a Brain."

ROSIE O'DONNELL REVEALS SHE WILL RETURN TO 'THE VIEW' FOR ANNIVERSARY, DETAILS TENSION WITH WHOOPI GOLDBERG

"I wanted to do that on Kimmel, but they just told me I can't, that they couldn’t get permission for the parody because it’s political content. And I was like, 'Well, that is absurd to me because we used to do parodies every day on my show,'" O'Donnell said.

A source familiar with the situation informed Fox News Digital that the song has not yet been rejected but is instead in the process of copyright clearance.

Fox News Digital also reached out to the FCC for comment.

O'Donnell is set to host one week of episodes for Kimmel's talk show beginning Aug. 17 during the host's two-month vacation. Other guest hosts, according to Kimmel, will include Tiffany Haddish, Colman Domingo, Ike Barinholtz, Anthony Anderson and Jelly Roll.

In 2025, Carr issued a threat against ABC and its parent company Disney, citing the potential "avenues" the FCC could pursue after Kimmel sparked outrage for his comments regarding Charlie Kirk's assassination. After companies like Nexstar Media Group and Sinclair Broadcast Group vowed to ban "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" on its stations following his comments, Disney announced it would preempt his show "indefinitely" before the show eventually returned to air one week later.

ABC FIRES BACK AT FCC PROBE OF 'THE VIEW,' CALLS OUT AGENCY'S 'CHILLING EFFECT ON FIRST AMENDMENT'

In an interview with Fox News Digital in February, Carr said that he feels "no regrets" for his original comments and instead felt glad that local stations and affiliates pushed back against corporations like Disney.

"In fact, I want to see more of that," Carr said. "I think these local affiliates have become simply mouthpieces in too many cases for Disney and other national programmers. I don't think we're better off as a country for that. And so I really want to see those local TV stations actually serve the needs of their community."

item.title: WNBA silent on Clay Travis offer to pay Las Vegas Aces $10 million to beat high school boys team
item.description: WNBA and WNBA champions both silent in response to Clay Travis offer of $10 million to the Las Vegas Aces to play a high school boys basketball team.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA has once again found itself embroiled in controversy, thanks in large part to the reaction from Sophie Cunningham's comments on male competition in women's sports.

When Cunningham said that transgender male athletes should not compete in women's sports, she echoed a position shared by 80% to 90% of the American public. And also one supported by the realities of biology and science considering the inherent physical advantages men have over women.

But her remarks set off a firestorm of criticism and backlash within the WNBA. Players, coaches, fans... all rushed to critique those comments, boo Cunningham whenever she touched the ball, or wear pointed clothing specifically in response to her statement. Several feigned ignorance of the science behind males in women's sports. One co-owner was even suspended after confronting a young Cunningham supporter.

CLAY TRAVIS UPS OFFER TO $10 MILLION FOR WNBA CHAMPION LAS VEGAS ACES TO PLAY HIGH SCHOOL BOYS BASKETBALL TEAM

In order to educate those curiously uninformed coaches, OutKick founder Clay Travis publicly posted an offer to the WNBA: have the Las Vegas Aces, the league's championship winning team, play a high school state title-winning boys' basketball team, with $10 million at stake. Beat the boys, get $10 million. For a team with an estimated annual revenue of $33 million, that's a substantial sum of money. Forbes even estimated the Aces were worth $300 million in 2025, meaning the $10 million prize would represent about 3.3% of the franchise's valuation.

Yet more than 24 hours later, there's been radio silence. Both from the league, from those coaches who are more than ready to jump in to defend left-wing politics whenever necessary, and from the Aces themselves.

OutKick then reached out to both the WNBA and the Aces organization to ask whether they'd consider Travis' offer. And, as of the time of publishing, had received nothing but the same radio silence. Which raises the question: Why? Why not respond? Why not play the game? Travis posted an update on Tuesday that says there are teams "across the country" reaching out wanting to participate. While also revealing why the Aces won't.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

"High school boys teams across the country are reaching out wanting to play the WNBA champ Las Vegas Aces," he wrote. "But the Aces are silent. Tells you everything. They know they would get smoked. But men should definitely be allowed to play in their league per coaches. Such a joke."

That's precisely the problem. The league, the players, the coaches, the Aces... they all know what the outcome would be. Which doesn't mean that the WNBA isn't worth watching for its fans, or that the women who play in it aren't extremely talented athletes in their own right. But it's clear that the WNBA exists because there are differences between men and women. Nobody's asking them to downplay their own talent, they're asking for a sports league to acknowledge the most basic tenets of objective reality. And they can't do it, because their commitment to left-wing politics comes first.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Travis also posted asking why the "WNBA (won't) just issue a statement saying only players born as women are eligible to play in their league? The Olympics and women’s tennis have done it. Caitlin Clark asked the league to make a statement. Seems pretty easy to do. Why the silence?"

That's it. That's not an enormous lift. It's not an unreasonable ask. It's the only justifiable position to maintain competitive integrity. And they can't do it, and they won't do it. Losing to an elite high school boy's basketball team wouldn't be embarrassing. But their complete and utter silence sure is.

item.title: Neighbors say riders' screams from Universal coaster pierce their windows day and night
item.description: Angry residents say screaming from riders on Universal Studios Hollywood's new "Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift" roller coaster echoes through their neighborhood day and night.
item.content:encoded:
Universal Studios Hollywood's new "Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift" roller coaster is already drawing complaints from nearby residents over its noise as the attraction undergoes technical rehearsals ahead of its official opening. 

Capable of reaching speeds of up to 72 mph, the outdoor coaster has brought backlash from neighbors, who say screams from test riders have echoed across the nearby Toluca Lake community, as Fox 11 Los Angeles reported.

A Universal Studios Hollywood spokesperson told Fox News Digital the venue is actively reviewing sound levels as technical rehearsals continue. It said the company values feedback from nearby residents.

NEW JERSEY COASTAL CITY CLASHES OVER PROPOSAL TO TRANSFORM AMUSEMENT PARK INTO LUXURY HOTEL

"We appreciate hearing from the community, and that feedback is an important part of the process," a Universal Studios Hollywood spokesperson said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital. 

"The coaster is currently in technical rehearsals. As part of that process, we are actively reviewing sound levels."

The more than 4,100-foot attraction is Universal Studios Hollywood's first high-speed outdoor roller coaster. It uses 360-degree rotating ride vehicles inspired by the "Fast & Furious" film franchise, according to Universal Studios Hollywood’s website.

During employee previews and technical rehearsals, residents said the noise was difficult to ignore, according to Fox 11 Los Angeles.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"I mean, when you're sitting outside, you just hear the screaming all throughout the day and then even into the night, so it's pretty non-stop," one resident told the outlet.

Another neighbor described the noise as "extremely disruptive."

"It not only echoes, it blasts all over the golf course and into the neighborhood," the resident said. 

"We all understand it's a giant studio that cares about making money, but at what cost [does it] destroy a beautiful neighborhood? It's ridiculous."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The noise complaints have also led to debate online. Many social media users argued that living next to a long-established theme park comes with the expectation of noise.

"You chose to live next to a theme park. Amusement things are noisy," one Reddit user wrote.

"[It's] the same type of people who move near an airport, then complain about airplane noise," another user added.

Others said they understood why residents were frustrated.

"I do kinda get it, as just hearing screams every 40 seconds all day would get annoying," another commenter wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The ride is expected to officially open sometime this summer, Universal Studios Hollywood’s website indicates.

item.title: Senators coach reveals that even he was surprised by team's blockbuster Brady Tkachuk trade
item.description: Travis Green admits he was surprised and even a little mad when Brady Tkachuk was traded to the Florida Panthers after taking the Ottawa Senators job.
item.content:encoded:
One of the most shocking parts of this NHL offseason — and there have been a few of them — came when the Ottawa Senators shipped captain Brady Tkachuk down to the Florida Panthers.

It came just weeks after Tkachuk insisted he was committed to the team.

And, in fact, it was so shocking, even Senators head coach Travis Green says he was surprised by it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"It was probably about a month after the season, three weeks that (Senators GM Steve Staios) brought me up to speed, and he asked me if I was surprised," Green recalled during an appearance on Daren Millard and John Shannon's 100% Hockey podcast. "Oh man, a little bit, of course."

Green — who previously coached the Vancouver Canucks and New Jersey Devils — said that the Senators' young core, which included Tkachuk, was one of the reasons he took the job in the Canadian capital.

So to hear that he had asked to be traded and he was going to be moved at some point — you know, unfortunate is a word I probably will use a lot," Green said. "I can't speak for Brady; I was a little surprised; a little, you know, would I say mad? A little bit."

Honestly, can you blame him?

SOCIAL MEDIA REACTS TO RED WINGS AWKWARDLY WISHING DYLAN LARKIN A HAPPY BIRTHDAY AFTER HE REQUESTED A TRADE

While things had gotten tough for Tkachuk at the end of his time in Ottawa, there's no question that the Sens are a team on the rise. They made the playoffs this season, and while they got waxed by the eventual champion Carolina Hurricanes (honestly, who didn't though this year), it showed a serious step in the right direction.

So, to lose a centerpiece like Tkachuk is tough.

But...

There's no question that, whether it was legitimate or fueled by the media, the attention around Tkachuk's status with the team was a distraction.

One that the team doesn't have any longer.

So, perhaps that will help them make another run to the playoffs again. The team brought in Andre Burakovsky and William Eklund, which rounds out a solid lineup that includes Tim Stützle, Drake Batherson, Shane Pinto, Jake Sanderson, Dylan Cozens and some veteran leadership from Claude Giroux, who signed a one-year deal to return to Ottawa last month.

item.title: Air Force says two advanced stealthy aircraft are ahead of schedule, with first delivery set for 2027
item.description: The B-21 Raider stealth bomber program accelerated 25% after a $4.5 billion funding boost, with Northrop Grumman targeting seven bombers annually.
item.content:encoded:
The Air Force says its next-generation B-21 Raider stealth bomber program is ahead of schedule, with the first operational aircraft expected to arrive at Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota in 2027.

The service's sixth-generation F-47 fighter is also progressing faster than expected, according to Gen. Dale White, director of Critical Major Weapon Systems, who discussed both programs during the Air Force's Life Cycle Industry Days conference in Dayton, Ohio.

White said the B-21 acquisition program has accelerated by roughly 25% since a one-time $4.5 billion funding boost was included in the 2025 reconciliation bill.

The comments provide one of the clearest public updates yet on the status of the Air Force's two flagship next-generation aircraft programs.

AMERICA’S NEW STEALTH B-21 RAIDER TAKES NEXT STEP WITH SECOND BOMBER’S FIRST FLIGHT

The update comes months after the Air Force announced a second B-21 Raider joined flight testing at Edwards Air Force Base in California, a milestone officials at the time said would accelerate testing and weapons integration for America's first new long-range bomber in more than three decades.

White said the first operational B-21 is expected to be "on the ramp" at Ellsworth in 2027, with Northrop Grumman planning to eventually produce seven operational bombers annually. The Pentagon has requested $6.1 billion for the B-21 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget proposal.

Built by Northrop Grumman, the B-21 is designed to carry both conventional and nuclear weapons while penetrating advanced enemy air defenses. The aircraft is expected to eventually replace the B-1 Lancer and B-2 Spirit while operating alongside modernized B-52 Stratofortress bombers expected to remain in service into the middle of the century. The Air Force plans to acquire at least 100 B-21 bombers.

White also said planning for the Boeing-built F-47 has reached an "unprecedented maturity."

INSIDE AMERICA’S 6TH-GEN ARSENAL: B-21, F-47, AND THE FUTURE OF AIR DOMINANCE

The Air Force plans to acquire 185 F-47 fighters, with the first flight scheduled for 2028. The aircraft will replace the F-22 Raptor as the service's primary air superiority fighter and is expected to operate alongside Collaborative Combat Aircraft, autonomous "loyal wingman" drones designed to support crewed aircraft in combat. The Pentagon has requested $5.03 billion for the F-47 program in its fiscal year 2027 budget request.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Air Force, Northrop Grumman and Boeing for comment.

item.title: WNBA coach torches league’s officiating after latest bizarre no-call: ‘It’s a f------ joke’
item.description: Tyler Marsh called it a joke after Kamilla Cardoso took 15 shots without a single free throw, adding to growing frustration over WNBA officiating.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Sky head coach Tyler Marsh didn’t attempt to hide his frustration with WNBA officials following Monday night’s loss to the Phoenix Mercury.

Marsh was asked how Kamilla Cardoso, a 6-foot-7 center, managed to play 28 minutes, take 15 shots and battle inside throughout the game without attempting a single free throw.

"That was a joke. It’s a f------ joke. It’s a joke," Marsh said. "How many more games does she need to go without getting a free throw? It makes no sense. Zero sense."

Cardoso finished with 16 points, 13 rebounds and five assists in Chicago’s 106-101 loss. She made eight of her 15 field-goal attempts, but never went to the line. The Mercury attempted 40 free throws compared to 25 for the Sky.

CAITLIN CLARK CALLS FOR FULL-TIME WNBA REFEREES AS OFFICIATING FAILURES MOUNT IN 2026

Marsh made clear that he wasn’t blaming the officials for the loss or suggesting Phoenix received 40 undeserved attempts. In fact, he admitted Chicago had been too undisciplined defensively.

"We fouled our asses off today. We could have been more disciplined," Marsh said. "Not saying the officials made 40 wrong calls or 20 wrong calls, whatever it is. Not saying that at all."

His complaint centered on Cardoso, who averages nearly 10 field-goal attempts per game but fewer than four free-throw attempts despite operating primarily around the basket. Marsh has raised the issue repeatedly and said last week that "the film doesn’t lie" about the amount of contact Cardoso absorbs.

Perhaps Marsh is exaggerating when he argues Cardoso should get close to 11 free throws every night. Coaches advocate for their players. That’s part of the job.

But zero?

That’s difficult to explain, particularly in a league that has spent much of the season trying to explain its officiating.

Marsh’s outburst might be dismissed as one frustrated coach defending one of his players if it happened in a vacuum. But it didn’t.

In June, Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas drove her fist into Caitlin Clark’s throat during a scramble for a loose ball. The officials didn’t call a foul.

The WNBA reviewed the play the following day, determined Thomas had committed a "non-basketball act," assessed a Flagrant Foul 2 and suspended her for one game.

In other words, the league decided the play was serious enough to warrant an ejection-level penalty and a suspension, but three officials watching it happen in real time didn’t see anything.

Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White called the no-call "absolutely egregious and utterly disrespectful."

The WNBA’s decision to punish Thomas after the fact validated White’s criticism. It also raised an obvious question: How does a player get struck in the throat in front of multiple officials without one of them blowing a whistle?

Then, on Sunday, Sophie Cunningham took an elbow to the face from Minnesota Lynx forward Nia Coffey.

Referees called a foul against Cunningham.

Officials reviewed the play but didn’t change the initial call, leaving the foul assessed to Cunningham despite her being the player who took an elbow to the mouth.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TAKES VICIOUS ELBOW TO FACE, AND FANS FUME AT WHAT REFS DID NEXT

Clark is the biggest draw in the league and Cunningham has become one of its most recognizable and polarizing players. Yet, WNBA officials missed a fist to Clark’s throat and managed to penalize Cunningham for getting hit in the face.

Now Marsh is publicly asking how Cardoso, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, can spend an entire game operating around the basket without earning one free throw.

The league knows officiating has become a problem and major errors involving some of the league's biggest stars are drawing more attention to the issue.

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert devoted a significant portion of her All-Star media availability to the issue, acknowledging that the league "always" needs to improve its officiating.

She said the league reviews every call, non-call and significant non-call, and announced that the WNBA plans to launch a fully centralized replay center in 2027.

Engelbert said the investment, which will cost tens of millions of dollars, is intended to create more consistency, efficiency and transparency.

That sounds good. It also doesn’t do much for players getting hit in the throat or face in 2026.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

The WNBA hasn’t committed to implementing the NBA’s Last Two Minute reports, which publicly identify correct and incorrect calls in the closing minutes of close games. So, while the league promises more transparency through a replay center next season, it still isn’t prepared to offer the type of public officiating accountability its NBA counterpart already provides.

Replay has its limits, too. Officials reviewed the Cunningham play and still left the foul on the player who got elbowed. The Clark play never even reached an in-game review.

A centralized replay center won’t fix much if officials fail to review obvious contact in the first place, or review it and still get the call wrong.

Marsh wasn’t arguing that officiating cost Chicago the game Monday. White’s complaints didn’t change the result of Indiana’s loss to Phoenix, either. But that’s not the point.

The issue is that coaches, players and fans continue to watch obvious contact treated completely differently from one game to the next.

Heck, sometimes it seems like the rules change from one possession to the next.

A replay center might help in 2027.

For now, the WNBA has a player punched in the throat with no foul, another called for a foul after taking an elbow to the face and a 6-foot-7 center who couldn’t get to the line once while taking nearly all her shots in the paint.

Marsh called it a "f------ joke."

At this point, he’s hardly alone.

item.title: Dirty text messages uncovered during investigation into married prison guard accused of affair with inmate
item.description: Jordan Pensak, a married federal prison guard at Fort Dix, faces sexual abuse charges after explicit messages revealed an alleged affair with an inmate.
item.content:encoded:
We've been here before. We've had married prison guards in hot water for alleged affairs with inmates. A lot of these tales of following one's heart into situations they can't win have taken place overseas.

This one is unraveling closer to home. At the center of the investigation is a 27-year-old married federal prison guard who worked at the Federal Correctional Institution in Fort Dix, New Jersey.

Yes, that is the same facility Sean "Diddy" Combs is currently calling home as he serves out his 50-month sentence. But this isn’t about him.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

This is about Jordan Pensak, who was charged last week with sexual abuse after dirty messages were uncovered during an investigation into her alleged affair with an inmate, reports the NY Post.

There was talk of "vibrating panties" and "big man hands" in one of the alleged dirty exchanges, according to the criminal complaint.

Pensak is alleged to have started the intimate relationship with the unnamed inmate sometime after she started working in his unit in 2024. They're accused of having sex in an office with paid inmates serving as lookouts.

Explicit messages as well as pictures and videos were reportedly found on the inmate's phone and on Pensak's phone after they were seized by investigators.

This one has it all. There was a pregnancy scare mentioned in the criminal complaint as well as text messages with someone believed to be a former inmate in which Pensak allegedly described graphic sex acts.

She also, the complaint states, complained to this person about their current lookout situation since he left.

She's alleged to have written in early 2026, "the lookout knocked on the door and opened it without us saying shit and he almost seen dick swanginnn."

That close call with a "swanginnn" sighting by a lookout evidently wasn't enough to slow these two down.

Pensak has been placed on administrative leave pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings, a spokesperson for the Federal Bureau of Prisons told The Post. She faces a maximum of 15 years if convicted.

The US Attorney's Office for New Jersey said she's been released on bail after being charged with sexual abuse.

This is a reminder that there's no place for romance to hide. These two found each other somehow and made memories. Memories that have landed the married prison guard into a lot of trouble.

Perhaps in another setting they could have had it all. I think this alleged text message from Pensak to the former inmate she reached out to sums it up: "Only thing he wont do is let me in them cheeks."

item.title: El-Sayed pals around with far-left streamer Hasan Piker the day before crucial Michigan Senate election
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed spent the night before the crucial election at a pool party alongside far-left streamer Hasan Piker.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed spent the night before Election Day at a pool party with far-left streamer Hasan Piker, sparking pushback from both his primary opponent and his Republican opposition.

The event was hosted by a content creator in Detroit, Michigan, and was attended by progressive House candidates Melat Kiros and Chris Rabb, both members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), The Associated Press reported.

Michigan Democratic state Rep. Donavan McKinney was also reportedly in attendance.

HASAN PIKER'S DEFENSE OF HAMAS HAVING 'RIGHT TO RESIST MILITARILY' DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM HUMAN RIGHTS GROUPS

Piker, who has roughly 10 million followers across multiple social media platforms, has made multiple appearances on the campaign trail with El-Sayed, raising questions about the ideological similarities between the two. 

Last month, Piker drew backlash after addressing a group of college students while wearing an outfit resembling that of former communist dictator Mao Zedong.

"I never would and never will criticize Mao Zedong," Piker said earlier this year in a clip that recently resurfaced on social media. "One of the great leaders of this world."

Piker has also said in the past that "America deserved 9/11" and has made controversial comments about Hamas and the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

While El-Sayed has said he doesn't agree with all of Piker’s positions, he has faced criticism for not distancing himself from the controversial streamer.

Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., running against El-Sayed in Tuesday night's Senate primary, was asked about the relationship between El-Sayed and Piker in a press gaggle hours before polls closed.

"I don't believe Mr. Piker lives here in our state. I do think his rhetoric should be denounced. I do think that my opponent should distance himself from him. I don't know what they were doing last night at this pool party that was going on, but I was with Congresswoman Hillary Scholten and Debbie Stabenow," Stevens told Fox News.

Referring to Piker, Stevens said, "Some of this stuff makes people uncomfortable. Frankly, it makes me uncomfortable. You know, we don't need these demagogues or people citing allegiance to Mao coming into Michigan."

And pointing to El-Sayed, Stevens added, "Maybe instead of being with Mr. Piker, you know, if he ends up winning the nomination, maybe he'll come with me and hear from some of the small businesses who don't want this extreme politics coming into our state."

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

"Instead of spending his final hours campaigning with Michiganders, Abdul El-Sayed spent it poolside with an antisemite and terrorist sympathizer who believes America deserved 9/11," NRSC regional press secretary Samantha Cantrell told Fox News Digital in a statement Tuesday.

The campaign of presumptive GOP nominee Mike Rogers also weighed in as voters headed to the polls Tuesday.

"We’re getting ready to prosecute the case against Abdul, but it looks like he’s already giving us a head start," Alyssa Brouillet, Rogers' campaign communications director, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This is giving fraud, not serious. And Michiganders are battling serious issues they need a senator to deal with — not someone who dances around with LA and NYC influencers who think ‘America deserved 9/11.’"

Hours before the pool party, Piker was at a campaign event with El-Sayed where a reporter asked him if he plans to campaign with the progressive Senate candidate after Tuesday night’s primary.

JAMES CARVILLE VOWS TO ABANDON DEMOCRATIC PARTY IF FAR-LEFT HASAN PIKER BECOMES LEADING VOICE

"Are you crazy?" Piker responded. "Of course."

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign and Piker’s team for comment.

El-Sayed squares off against Stevens in the Michigan Democratic Senate primary Tuesday night, where polls close at 8 p.m. El-Sayed, according to recent polling, is expected to advance to the general election in November to face Rogers in a race that could determine the balance of power in the U.S. Senate.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment by the time of publication.

item.title: 'Spider-Man' showing was reportedly evacuated due to someone's uncontrolled gas release
item.description: A packed Colombia theater showing "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" was reportedly evacuated after someone's nonstop farts made it truly uninhabitable.
item.content:encoded:
The last time I went to the movies, there was a group of teenagers sitting a row behind me who talked through the entire movie.

"Man, this has to be the worst bit of poor social etiquette that could ever happen in a movie theater," I remember thinking, as I tried to block it out and zero in on the finer plot points of "Minions and Monsters" (which was great, by the way).

Well, according to reports coming from a showing of "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" in Colombia, I was mistaken.

'SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY' REVIEW: TOM HOLLAND, ZENDAYA RETURN FOR ACTION-PACKED, EMOTIONAL SEQUEL

According to The New York Post, someone had to pull the e-brake on a showing of the latest Tom Holland-led Spider-Man flick because someone in the theater just could not stop dropping more gaseous bombs than the Green Goblin.

This is just absurd...

You get one fart, maybe a second if I'm feeling generous with the benefit of the doubt, but enough to clear a packed theater?

No. Unacceptable. Not in my America... or Colombia.

And not just any theater. A theater full of Marvel nerds.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

A mouse gasser could clear out an arthouse theater, but if you've ever been to a comic book convention, you'll know that those folks are willing to put up with a lot on the olfactory front.

So for them to be like, "This is too much, we must bail," it must have meant that theater was truly uninhabitable.

I'm not sure what the theater looked like, but it makes me wonder if this was the kind of theater with recliners. I've been saying for a long time that modern theaters are getting too comfortable.

I don't like the big cushy couches. It makes people feel too comfortable, too at home.

What happens when you feel that way? Someone clears out an entire auditorium of paying customers.

Give me old-fashioned seats any day of the week.

Sure, you might leave with a lower back ache, but at least someone's ass won't chase you out of the theater before the credits start rolling.

item.title: Women's advocacy groups respond to Caitlin Clark's answer on demonstrations at Fever games
item.description: Multiple groups react to Caitlin Clark's response about trans athletes in women's sports, with some expressing disappointment in her neutral stance.
item.content:encoded:
Caitlin Clark's answer to a question about the WNBA's convergence with the "Save Women's Sports" movement became a point of internal debate within the movement and her fan base in recent days.

Dave Portnoy and Megyn Kelly, two known Clark supporters, even went at it on X about it.

Clark was asked Sunday about the WNBA's ongoing controversy related to demonstrations outside of Indiana Fever games. Her teammate Sophie Cunningham voiced her support for protecting women's sports from biological males in late July, and rallies in support of Cunningham have followed the Fever to their last three games. Counterprotests have also appeared outside each of the last three games.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Clark did not reveal her stance on the issue when she answered, but deferred to the governing bodies and leagues that oversee women's sports.

"I think, for us, it's not really a discussion we really have in our locker room," Clark answered. "I think it's for leagues and the governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. Our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and, obviously, we didn't do that tonight. So we need to find an area to improve in that way."

Clark then declined a related follow-up question, saying "I just answered for you."

Multiple advocacy groups leading the "Save Women's Sports" movement have addressed Clark's answer in statements to Fox News Digital.

Some of the groups appeared to defend Clark.

"Female athletes should never be forced to 'pick a side' to defend their right to the same opportunities afforded to men or be pressured to surrender that right in the middle of their careers. Yet because sport leaders have failed to adopt clear, fair policies, players are left carrying that burden themselves, creating unnecessary conflict among teammates, friends, and competitors," ICONS co-founder Marshi Smith told Fox News Digital.

SJSU VOLLEYBALL SCANDAL PROBE FINDS TEAM ALLEGEDLY RECRUITED MALE FOR ADVANTAGE WITHOUT TELLING FEMALE PLAYERS

"We saw the devastating toll of this during the Mountain West volleyball controversy, where women were placed in the impossible position of choosing between standing up for what they believed was fair or forfeiting games at the expense of their teams.

"The resulting tension fractured relationships and divided women’s teams. That division was not created by the athletes. It was the product of institutional failure. Women’s leagues should be for women. It is the responsibility of sport leaders, not individual players, to protect the integrity of women’s competition so athletes can focus on what they came to do: compete. But when policymakers fail women, courage falls to the athletes. History has always revealed the difference between the timid and the bold, between those captive to ideology and those willing to stand for what is right."

"Everyone should be able to make the point that a women's league should be for women. This shouldn't be hard. It’s understandable that Caitlin Clark wants to dodge this question because the leadership of her league has been so embarrassing in their response," Independent Women President Carrie Lukas told Fox News Digital.

"That's a disservice to every female professional basketball player and every young girl who hopes to play in the future. Of course, men shouldn't be allowed in women's basketball. Full stop. You can support both equality and protecting women's sports for females only. That's why the women's basketball league exists."

THESE FEMALE ATHLETES NEED TO SPEAK UP ABOUT KEEPING WOMEN'S SPORTS FOR WOMEN, LIKE SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DID

"Caitlin Clark had an opportunity to stand up for women and girls, and she chose not to. This isn't a question that should be punted or treated as someone else's responsibility. Female athletes deserve leaders and role models willing to say what the science, common sense, and now the U.S. Supreme Court have recognized: sex matters in sports," Independent Women’s Law Center senior legal counsel Beth Parlato told Fox News Digital.

"Protecting women's sports isn't controversial; it is essential to preserving fairness, safety, and equal athletic opportunity for female athletes. More athletes need to take a stand like Sophie Cunningham has and have the courage to speak clearly in defense of the very category that made their own success possible."

"Athletes like Sophie Cunningham who are standing up for women and girls to have fair competition are exceptional and courageous. We hope that Clark and every other WNBA player will stand up in support of female athletes. But ultimately, the WNBA and other sports governing bodies must facilitate fair and safe competitions so their athletes can focus on competing. The WNBA should immediately adopt a policy that establishes only biological women can play basketball in the league. Does the WNBA stand for fairness in women’s sports or not?" Concerned Women for America CEO and President Penny Nance told Fox News Digital.

"Women in the public eye have a responsibility to set an example for the young girls watching them, and that starts with standing up for the fundamentals of basic biology. It should never be difficult to defend common sense, and it should never be controversial to protect young girls. Every woman with a platform has a choice: stand up for the next generation of girls, or stay silent while their opportunities, their privacy, and their safety are taken away. Parents across America know where Moms for Liberty stands, and we will never back down." Moms for Liberty CEO and Co-Founder of Moms for Liberty Tina Descovich told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Hasan Piker, Abdul El-Sayed mock James Carville threatening to leave Democrats and 'sweetening the deal'

item.title: Carrie Underwood is back for SNF, Angel Reese celebrates Barbie Night & NFL WAGs are training-camp ready
item.description: Carrie Underwood returns for her 14th season performing the "Sunday Night Football" theme, while NFL WAGs send husbands off to training camp.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy to report I am back in the beautiful state of Tennessee.

The husband, dog and I had a nice time on our pilgrimage to the Great White North, but I am happy to be back in my own cozy home, sleeping on my own elite mattress and caring for my own little house plants.

And there's much to do now that I'm back.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

We have some exciting things coming up in OutKick Outdoors. No spoilers, but if you're into hunting, fishing, hiking, camping or even just drinking beer on patios, you should definitely be following us on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

Ain't too proud for a shameless plug, baby.

But that's enough of that for now. We've got some Nightcaps to do.

There's an old saying that goes, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it."

And that's exactly why NBC invited back Carrie Underwood to perform the theme song ahead of Sunday Night Football — for the 14th season in a row.

I mean, who else are you gonna get? That lady from the Women’s Pro Baseball League?

It's like they pulled three random drunk women out of a crowd and handed them microphones.

Point is, Carrie Underwood is a crowd pleaser. So come September, she and her glorious legs (I say that as an entirely straight woman) will — once again — bless our TV screens before we watch someone play against the Dallas Cowboys or Kansas City Chiefs.

Seriously, those teams make three SNF appearances each this season. You know who doesn't get any Carrie Underwood games? The Dolphins, Jets and Raiders.

Womp.

Not that I blame the schedule-makers there. I'm a Dolphins fan, and even I believe no one should be subjected to that dumpster fire in prime time.

Fun game of would you rather: three hours of Miami Dolphins football or the Martha Reeves national anthem on repeat?

Faced with that option, it almost makes Malik Washington to Jalen Tolbert sound exhilarating.

Anyway, Carrie's ready. I'm ready. You're ready. Let's get to September already.

You know who else is ready for football season? The NFL WAGs, who are pushing their boyfriends and husbands out of the house for a few weeks of uninterrupted quiet time during training camp.

Back when I worked for the Titans, anyone with fewer than three seasons (I think that was the cutoff) in the league had to stay at the Millennium Maxwell House. What a s— hole that was. It sounds fancy, but I promise: certified s— hole.

One time one of our running backs got bed bugs there, and the whole place had to be fumigated. Then, all the players lined up in a queue of shame to dump all of their worldly belongings into the laundry bin at the facility.

I was careful not to touch anything in the locker room that week. No creepy crawlies in my house, thank you.

I don't know how the Titans do training camp now, but I hope — for the players' sake — they found nicer accommodations. Or let them live at home.

Here's Drew Allar's girlfriend stocking him up with all the snacks he'll need to back up Aaron Rodgers.

Here's Isaiah Likely's wife, Melanie, sending him off in style.

Here's Myles Garrett's girlfriend — Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim — passive aggressively wishing herself a happy National Girlfriends Day since Myles apparently forgot to.

To be fair, he's trying to learn a whole new playbook out there in LA. Also, no sane person on planet earth knows when National Girlfriend Day is.

And finally, here's Jaxson Dart's girlfriend, Marissa Ayers, who has no time to care about football right now. Because it's summer, and she's in Oahu.

This is probably no news to you. Because I'm sure you've had it in your calendar for months. But the Atlanta Dream held a Barbie theme night for Angel Reese.

It was either to celebrate the release of her special edition Barbie Doll or her Barbie pink signature Reebok shoes. Or both, I don't know.

Say what you want about the woman, but she is printing money.

Angel said this Barbie collaboration means a lot to her because when she was growing up, there weren't a lot of dolls who "looked like her" and hooped like her.

Of course, she's insinuating there weren't Black dolls. Or Black dolls who played basketball. Which is just categorically false. I'm older than Angel Reese (by more than a couple years), and dolls of all skin colors were readily available when I was a kid.

ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN

As a user on Twitter / X pointed out today, Christie, Barbie's Black friend, entered Barbie’s world in 1968. The first official Black Barbie arrived in 1980. And in 1998, four years before Reese was born, Mattel was already selling Black basketball-playing Barbie dolls in authentic NBA uniforms.

If you ask me (and no one did), the real injustice is the shortage of brunette Barbies. For much of my childhood, I had to settle for Barbie's less popular friend Teresa. Where is my representation?! Where is my theme night?!

I'm in the weeds. Good for Angel and her doll and her signature shoe, I guess.

Apparently, Barbie Night was a real star-studded event at State Farm Arena — with celebrities like Flo Milli, Dess Dior and Chaylyn, the OMG Girlz, Saucy Santana and Mariah the Scientist (who I'm almost certain is not a real scientist) all in the building.

Look, I know I live three hours from Atlanta, but I honestly could not tell you who a single one of those people are — aside from Michael Harris, who plays for the Braves.

I'm glad they had a nice time, though.

Football season is around the corner, which means so is your fantasy draft.

And you better take it seriously or else you might end up forced to take the last-place punishment.

We've heard all the popular ones:

And then, there's this:

As someone who used to compete in bodybuilding shows, I can promise you that standing up on stage — nearly naked with an ungodly spray tan — and performing a posing routine is one of the more terrifying and humbling things you'll ever do in your lifetime.

Or never do, if you're smart.

And don't even get me started on the intense cardio, training and dieting you have to do for months ahead of time in order to look like you belong. Alternatively, I guess you can just say "f— it," trot on out there, and shamelesslystrut what the good Lord gave you. Like this guy did.

So is this the worst fantasy football punishment ever? Or can you top it?

Let me know.

item.title: Alarming missile report draws forceful response from Trump as Iran war tests America’s arsenal
item.description: A report says the Army has burned through virtually all ATACMS and PrSM stocks during the Iran conflict, raising fears about future crises.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is rejecting concerns that the war with Iran has left the U.S. low on some of its most advanced long-range missiles, after a report found the Army burned through "virtually all" of its stocks of two of its primary long-range precision weapons.

The Army has used "virtually all" of its inventories of Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM) during the five-month conflict with Iran, Reuters, citing people familiar with internal U.S. military data, reported Tuesday. Officials fear the drawdown could complicate the military's ability to respond to future crises involving adversaries such as China and Russia, according to the report.

The White House disputed any suggestion the U.S. military lacks the weapons needed to carry out its missions.

WEAPONS STOCKPILE SHORTAGES IMPACTING MILITARY STRATEGY IN THE MIDEAST

"We have far more munitions than anyone in the world, and far more than we need, despite the fact that an unprecedented amount was given away by Crooked Joe Biden and the Biden Administration to Ukraine and Europe at no cost, in one of many of their extremely dumb moves," President Donald Trump said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our defense companies are, at this moment, making more munitions than they have ever made before, in addition to expanding their plants and equipment at record levels. And as we build up, we will start issuing more to our allies in Europe and elsewhere."

If accurate, the report underscores a longstanding Pentagon concern: America's most sophisticated precision weapons can be expended in months but often take years to replace.

Reuters also reported that the conflict significantly reduced inventories of Patriot and THAAD missile interceptors, along with Tomahawk cruise missiles, though the Pentagon has maintained the U.S. military retains the capabilities needed to carry out operations worldwide.

HEGSETH DISMISSES ‘FOOLISH’ US STOCKPILE CONCERNS AS IRAN CONFLICT TESTS MUNITIONS

Exact U.S. weapons stockpile figures remain classified for national security reasons.

The Pentagon also pushed back on the reporting. "America’s military is the most powerful in the world and has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the President’s choosing. We have executed multiple successful operations across combatant commands while ensuring the U.S. military possesses a deep arsenal of capabilities to protect our people and our interests," chief spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement.

Independent analysts have also warned that months of combat have strained U.S. inventories of high-end munitions. The Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated last week that the U.S. had expended roughly 65% of its Patriot interceptor stockpile and that inventories of THAAD interceptors had fallen by at least 38% since the start of the Iran conflict, based on open-source analysis and budget data. Reuters reported Tuesday that its sources said those figures broadly aligned with internal U.S. data.

ATACMS and the newer Precision Strike Missile are among the Army's premier long-range precision strike weapons, capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away without putting pilots in harm's way.

ARMY CUTS HELICOPTERS, PUSHES ‘AMAZON FOR WAR’ AS DRONE COMBAT RESHAPES MILITARY

Military planners consider them particularly valuable against heavily defended adversaries because they can destroy command posts, air defenses, logistics hubs and other high-value targets from beyond many enemy air-defense systems.

Patriot and THAAD serve a different mission. Rather than striking enemy targets, they defend U.S. forces and allies by intercepting incoming ballistic missiles, while Tomahawk cruise missiles allow the Navy to conduct long-range strikes from ships and submarines.

The report comes as Pentagon leaders have increasingly warned about the challenge of sustaining prolonged, high-intensity conflicts against major powers while replenishing advanced weapons consumed in combat.

That concern has accelerated efforts to pair expensive precision missiles with far larger numbers of lower-cost, "attritable" drones and autonomous systems that can be produced rapidly and fielded at scale. Officials argue the approach would allow commanders to reserve million-dollar precision weapons for the highest-value targets while relying on less expensive systems for surveillance, electronic warfare and many strike missions.

Military leaders caution, however, that inexpensive drones are not a replacement for long-range precision missiles such as ATACMS and PrSM. Those weapons remain essential for striking hardened command centers, air-defense batteries and other heavily defended targets at distances many lower-cost drones cannot yet reach or survive.

Trump has met repeatedly with executives from the nation's largest defense contractors, pressing them to accelerate production and expand manufacturing capacity as conflicts in Iran and Ukraine strain U.S. stockpiles.

Following a White House meeting in March, Trump said the companies had agreed to quadruple production of what he called "Exquisite Class Weaponry," including some of the military's most advanced missile systems. At a second meeting in June and again at a defense summit in July, the president urged industry leaders to move faster, telling executives, "We have the best quality in the world, but we need a little more speed."

The production push is also reflected in the administration's budget priorities. Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget would more than triple spending on drones and autonomous systems while boosting investment in munitions production, missile defense and Tomahawk cruise missile procurement.

item.title: Tennessee coach unloads on NCAA's 'bulls–t', after star linebacker suspended for outdated rule
item.description: Josh Heupel called the NCAA's two-game suspension of Arion Carter "bullsh*t," blasting outdated rules after the linebacker returned from the NFL Draft.
item.content:encoded:
KNOXVILLE, TN - After the NCAA decided it was going to suspend Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter for the opening two games of the upcoming season, his head coach did not hesitate to call out the organization for the current rule structure.

Following the 2025 season, Carter decided it was time to pursue his NFL dreams by declaring for the draft and hiring a professional agent to start the process. It was at that moment that the Tennessee linebacker lost his collegiate eligibility according to the antiquated rules currently in place.

Because Carter also accepted a $427 plane ticket from his professional agent to attend a training session, which is when the linebacker first discovered that he had suffered a foot injury that would prevent him from fully reaching his potential of being drafted high.

In reality, Arion would have lost millions because of the injury, so he decided the best course of action was a return to college, which transpired just weeks after he first initially announced his decision to go pro.

Carter also paid back the $427 and the school self-reported the 'violation' to the NCAA.

After informing Tennessee that he wanted to return, the question whether the Vols had a roster spot for him. So, he entered the transfer portal for a quick stop, before rejoining the Tennessee football program.

Speaking on Tuesday before the Vols open Fall camp, head coach Josh Heupel did not mince words on the NCAA's punishment of a 2-game suspension for the linebacker.

"He's done everything the right way..The ruling that came out from the NCAA of a 2-game suspension I truly believe is bullshit," Heupel fiercely noted. "You look at the landscape of college football, the rules of NIL and everything, I think the ruling is completely outdated. I am disappointed for him, and for us, with the result of that ruling."

item.title: Iran’s unseen supreme leader becomes weapon in escalating power struggle, experts say
item.description: Iran's rival factions invoke Mojtaba Khamenei's name to attack opponents, but his prolonged public absence raises questions about who governs.
item.content:encoded:
Iran’s rival political factions are increasingly invoking the authority of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to attack their opponents and protect their own positions, even as questions persist over whether he is actively governing the country, according to an Iran expert.

The internal struggle surfaced in two reports published by Iran International concerning Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s relationship with the new supreme leader.

In the first report, senior cleric Mohammad-Bagher Kharrazi, a relative of the Khamenei family by marriage, claimed Pezeshkian had repeatedly threatened to resign and was warned that his next resignation would be accepted.

IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE

"If he resigns one more time, I will approve it," Kharrazi quoted Khamenei as saying.

Pezeshkian’s office strongly denied the account. Mehdi Tabatabaei, the president’s deputy for communications and information, called the allegation "baseless and an outright lie," while another presidential advisor said Kharrazi had no contact with the supreme leader and was known for telling "strange stories."

Hours later, Iran International published a second report alleging Pezeshkian had met Mojtaba Khamenei only once, inside a vehicle with tinted windows at an undisclosed location in Tehran.

According to the outlet’s unnamed sources, the encounter lasted several minutes, the two men could not see each other and Pezeshkian was not permitted to shake Khamenei’s hand. The report alleged that the president later questioned whether the voice he heard had actually belonged to the supreme leader.

IRAN’S GOOD COP, BAD COP GAME IMPLODES AS EXPERTS WARN REGIME VIEWS US AS 'EVIL'

The claims have not been independently verified. Pezeshkian previously described a substantially different encounter, saying publicly that he had spent approximately two and a half hours with Khamenei in a cordial atmosphere.

Kasra Aarabi, director of IRGC research at United Against Nuclear Iran, said the competing claims surrounding Pezeshkian and Mojtaba Khamenei reflected a deeper struggle inside what he described as an "Islamist oligarchic mafia system."

Under Ali Khamenei, Aarabi said, the supreme leader functioned as the system’s "godfather," arbitrating among rival Islamist factions and guaranteeing their access to power and money. His removal created a vacuum that Mojtaba Khamenei’s appointment was intended to fill, but the new supreme leader’s prolonged public absence has left rival factions uncertain about who is actually in charge.

"The very essence of this mafia system is built on a godfather," Aarabi said. "If the godfather is absent, whether because he is severely incapacitated or nonexistent, that vacuum… re-emerges between the various Islamist oligarchic clans."

Aarabi said those factions are not primarily divided by ideology.

"They’re not competing over ideology," he said. "They’re competing over raw power and economic interests."

In that environment, Aarabi said, Mojtaba Khamenei’s name has become a political instrument that competing factions can invoke to legitimize themselves, constrain their rivals or justify decisions whose true source remains unclear.

WHO IS AHMAD VAHIDI? IRAN’S NEW IRGC CHIEF TIED TO GLOBAL ATTACKS AND ‘DEATH TO AMERICA’ IDEOLOGY

"Mojtaba’s name is the glue that’s holding the system together right now," Aarabi said. "Each of these clans invokes his name to justify its existence, legitimize its position, and consolidate its place within this fragile system."

Exiled Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi described the resignation claims as part of a recurring political strategy used by reformist administrations.

"This is a familiar cycle," Ghadimi said. "Whenever they feel that their usefulness to the supreme leader has come to an end, they start circulating these resignation rumors in an effort to build public sympathy and improve their image before being pushed aside."

Ghadimi said similar rumors surrounded former presidents Mohammad Khatami and Hassan Rouhani during the final years of their administrations. He argued that reformist-aligned media channels often continue circulating resignation claims even after a president’s office formally denies them, allowing officials later to portray themselves as having challenged the supreme leader.

On Mojtaba Khamenei’s status, Ghadimi went further than Aarabi, saying he did not believe there was "a functioning person by that name who is capable of thinking, making decisions or speaking."

"Either he is dead, or he is being kept alive in an extremely unstable and severely deteriorated condition," Ghadimi said.

Aarabi said the two reports illustrate that dynamic. A cleric opposed to or unaligned with Pezeshkian invoked Mojtaba Khamenei’s authority to weaken the president by claiming his next resignation would be accepted, while figures around Pezeshkian pushed back with an account portraying the president as having met directly with the supreme leader.

Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared in any publicly released video or audio recording since succeeding his father, according to Iran International. Iranian officials have offered conflicting accounts about how often senior government figures have met him.

Aarabi cautioned that using Khamenei’s name as a source of authority will become increasingly difficult if his public absence continues.

"There’s only so many times you can use someone’s name without any proof of life that they actually exist," Aarabi said. "The longer Mojtaba is absent, the more questions develop over whether he is alive or able. And as soon as that doubt increases, you will see this infighting increase."

item.title: Trump keeps calling Thune despite public fight over SAVE America Act
item.description: John Thune says Trump called him twice in one morning, pushing back on reports their working relationship over the SAVE America Act has collapsed.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The reports of President Donald Trump and Senate Majority Leader John Thune's dead working relationship have been greatly exaggerated, the South Dakota Republican leader told Fox News Digital.

"I've heard from him twice this morning already. He called me over the weekend, and so there, you know, we talk, I don't bother him, I'm not calling him every day," Thune said in an interview.

Last week, Trump said, "We're going to find out," whether Thune was the man for the job to lead Senate Republicans, casting doubt on a critical relationship between him and the Senate’s top Republican.

TRUMP QUESTIONS THUNE'S LEADERSHIP AS SAVE AMERICA ACT STALLS

The tension stems from the SAVE America Act floundering in the Senate, and Trump’s desire to see the election integrity package passed by any means necessary.

Thune doesn’t see Trump’s comment as a personal slight, however. Both he and the president "want to get to the same place. We have, sometimes, disagreements about how best to get there."

"Most of mine are constrained by what's achievable in an institution like the Senate that has procedural roadblocks to do almost anything," Thune said.

"We have those candid conversations, but I'm not worried about that relationship," he continued. "I know he's going to push as hard as he can. That's his business model, is to just keep pushing, pushing, pushing to get people to go as far as they can go."

SENATE FACES 'COME-TO-JESUS' MOMENT ON TRUMP'S ELECTION PRIORITY UNDER GOP'S NEW PLAN

There is a voracious appetite among Trump, Senate Republicans and their base to see the SAVE America Act passed. One that Thune hears every day, either online or within his own conference.

It’s dominated the oxygen inside the Capitol and beyond its walls, and the pressure comes as the Senate is sprinting to finish work on key items, like preventing a government shutdown and confirming dozens of Trump’s nominees.

"There are good days and bad days," Thune said. "And around here, probably lately more bad days than good days, but you know you just kind of, like I said, keep your head down, do the work."

But passing the SAVE America Act is the most elusive item for Republicans, given the current make up of the Senate.

While there are a cohort of Republicans who are voting against it, Thune made the point that every single Senate Democrat has shut it down each of the five times that it’s been brought to the floor in a variety of configurations.

And Thune is one of the Republicans that wants the bill passed — he’s an original co-sponsor of the SAVE Act, the precursor to the current version of the SAVE America Act. The avenue of cutting Democrats out of the equation and ramming through aspects of the bill through budget reconciliation exists, which Thune is interested in pursuing.

But then comes the problem of generating 50 votes to support that, and keeping those votes together to shut down "crazy democratic amendments."

GOP RIFT GROWS AS THUNE HITS BRAKES ON TRUMP'S ELECTION BILL TO AVERT SHUTDOWN

Thune's job helming the Senate majority is to do the math on what can be accomplished in an institution that’s "designed" to be difficult. And the votes still aren’t adding up.

"I keep asking the question, am I the only one in this town that can count to 50? Because it seems like these questions recur and there are a lot of people out there who haven't seemed to internalize the fact that there aren't Democrats that are going to flip and vote for this," Thune said.

"And there aren't 50 Republicans that are going to vote to nuke the filibuster. Those are two facts that are indisputable and unchangeable."

Thune’s position is, by extension, an embodiment of the Senate in many ways.

Unlike the House, legislation and agendas can’t be rammed through without a bipartisan agreement to blast through the filibuster. And senators' concerns and desires encompass an entire state, not just a sliver of a state’s population.

Through several interviews with Fox News Digital, he’s instilled that part of his job is to listen and take consensus on what does and doesn’t work, deliberating on the best path for a deliverable outcome.

"This place was supposed to be difficult, so that no dictator could master it, and I think that's kind of the role of the Senate in our system and our democracy," Thune said.

"It's important to keep that in perspective, but it's frustrating as heck when you're somebody who likes to get things done, likes to get results, and you've got procedural roadblocks holding things up as we try to wind down and get some things done," he continued.

"The allegations are unrelated to her duties with the Mount Vernon Police Department and do not stem from any conduct associated with the Department or the performance of her official responsibilities," the department wrote on social media.

The incident was far from Chase's first run-in with law enforcement. He was shot by police in 2024 after allegedly wielding a gun during an argument.

He was also shot once before in 2023 by three other youths during a dispute on a bus. Chase is allegedly a member of the "Slutty Gang," according to the Post.

He reportedly demanded to know what gang the other youths belonged to and then attempted to drag one of them off the bus before being shot in the chest.

item.title: Embattled GOP rep takes dramatic step to 'clear my name' as abuse allegations engulf House race
item.description: Rep. Max Miller filed for an ethics investigation into himself to clear his name as Sen. Bernie Moreno calls him a "danger" to his own family.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, is calling for an investigation into abuse allegations made against him by his ex-wife, as the dramatic family feud overshadows his race for re-election.

Miller has consistently denied wrongdoing and accused both his ex-wife and her father, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, of trying to take down his political career.

"In light of all the renewed interest in my family affairs, I am going to file my own paperwork for an ethics investigation into myself to clear my name from these horrific attacks on myself and my family. I have absolutely nothing to hide," Miller wrote on X on Tuesday.

"We will be providing the committee all necessary documents needed for a detail examination. The accusations continue to change, but my facts stay the same. I am looking forward to my colleagues reading everything for themselves."

OHIO GOP FAMILY FEUD EXPLODES AS SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS ON REP MAX MILLER TO RESIGN

The Ethics Committee confirmed on Tuesday afternoon that it would investigate allegations that Miller "may have engaged in domestic violence and abuse or illegal drug use."

Emily Moreno, who filed for divorce from Miller in 2024 after two years of marriage, has accused him of physically abusing both her and their young daughter. Allegations include that he scalded Moreno with boiling water and held a gun to her head during two separate occasions, and that she had to get their daughter medical aid for a broken collar bone after she was in Miller's care.

Miller suggested in a livestream on X over the weekend that Moreno had suffered from mental health issues in the past and that might be the reason behind her accusations. He also said none of the allegations she made have been substantiated by relevant entities.

"Every single one of these allegations were already investigated. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me," Miller said in the video. He said the water incident occurred during "horseplay" between the two, and disputed that the water was boiling. He also said Moreno took their daughter to the emergency room thinking there was a bruise on their daughter's neck, but that the mark was from finger painting.

SEN BERNIE MORENO CALLS FOR EX-SON-IN-LAW TO RESIGN FROM HOUSE, GET 'SERIOUS PSYCHOLOGICAL HELP'

But mounting public pressure has brought the Cleveland-area feud to Washington, where Sen. Moreno told reporters Tuesday that Miller "fails to meet that minimum basic standard" for elected officials who get to serve.

He also criticized Miller in a statement posted on X, calling him a "danger" to his daughter and granddaughter. Miller and Moreno share custody over the child.

The intense public scrutiny is also potentially putting Miller's re-election into question, with Democrats seeing new opportunity in what was a relatively safe red seat in the Cleveland suburbs.

One House GOP source, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about a sensitive situation, told Fox News Digital the situation was a "f—-ing trainwreck."

DEMOCRATS TARGET MORE GOP HOUSE SEATS AFTER SOCIALIST VICTORIES ROCK LEFT-WING PRIMARIES

The source noted that the allegations against Miller had not been substantiated, but said "the court of public opinion is a b—-."

Miller likely appears to voters to have "a little too much on his plate," the source said.

Meanwhile, a House Republican, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly, said Miller should not run for re-election. "We must lead by example," they said.

The same House Republican also called for Reps. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., and Cory Mills, R-Fla., also facing harassment allegations that they have denied, to similarly drop out of their races.

But Miller has been defiant so far, expressing confidence that he'll win in November.

The House Ethics Committee, which Miller is calling on to investigate his case, recently recommended that Edwards be censured for his behavior toward two young female staffers.
